newsitem.title: UK: Punter puts $17,850 on Labour UK election win.
newsitem.headline: Punter puts $17,850 on Labour UK election win.

text.p: A man who never placed a bet before has wagered more than 11,000 pounds stg ($18,000) on Britain's opposition Labour Party winning the May 1 election.
"The gentleman told staff he never normally had a bet but decided to splash out on a Labour win," Graham Sharpe, a spokesman for the William Hill betting chain, said in a statement.
The unidentified middle-aged punter bet exactly 11,467.89 pounds at odds of 1-6 on Labour ousting the ruling Conservatives after 18 years in power.

William Hill has also made veteran BBC war correspondent Martin Bell, who is running as an anti-sleaze candidate, a 4-6 favourite to defeat former minister Neil Hamilton for the Tatton seat in northwest England.
Hamilton is at the centre of the cash-for-questions scandal that has been dogging the ruling Conservatives. He denies taking money from a businessman in return for asking questions in parliament.
